_note: New staff by season, for engine/teamchange. A team listed for a season leans harder on that season's numbers on that side of the ball: hc -> both sides, oc -> offense, dc -> defense. Starting-QB changes come from the nflverse schedule and are not listed here; head coaches come from the schedule too, and are listed here as a backstop because nflverse can keep last season's coach on a season's rows (Arizona 2026 still read Jonathan Gannon in September). Only staff new THIS season, every name from a published report of the hire, never a guess. Left out on purpose: New England's Zak Kuhr (DC title in 2026, but he already ran the defense through 2025, so last season's numbers are his); coordinators retained under a new head coach (Arizona's Nick Rallis, Atlanta's Jeff Ulbrich). hc_calls: the side whose plays the HEAD COACH calls over a new coordinator (Jets defense: Aaron Glenn; Chiefs: Andy Reid; Bears: Ben Johnson; Rams: Sean McVay) — that side leans 60/40 on this season instead of 75/25, unless a new head coach or QB also changed it. Teams whose head coach calls plays but the new coordinator was given them are NOT marked (Broncos: Davis Webb calls; Seahawks, Buccaneers). Only teams where it changes the split are marked: a new head coach already moves both sides in full.
_sources: Compiled 2026-09-27 from published reports: Adam Schefter's list of the 21 new offensive coordinators (x.com/AdamSchefter/status/2024829911358173205); team announcements and NFL.com/ESPN/AP reports for each defensive coordinator and head coach hire (newyorkjets.com, baltimoreravens.com, miamidolphins.com, giants.com, buffalobills.com, clevelandbrowns.com, packers.com, dallascowboys.com, chargers.com, tennesseetitans.com, steelers.com, azcardinals.com, atlantafalcons.com; Washington Post on the 49ers and Titans; ESPN on the Raiders; Wikipedia's 2026 Washington Commanders season). Play callers: newyorkjets.com (Glenn will call the defense, 2026-02-24), ESPN's 32-team play-caller guide and Yahoo/Acme Packing Company (Reid, Johnson; Webb given Denver's calls), Turf Show Times (McVay calls, Scheelhaase once), Seahawks and Buccaneers reports of Fleury's and Robinson's play-calling debuts.
